To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) BOLD fMRI data acquired at multiple echo times (TEs) provide a more robust estimate of functional connectivity, 2) the effect of echo time on functional connectivity is dependent on the post-processing procedure applied to the BOLD data, 3) the effect of motion and physiological noise on functional connectivity is also dependent on echo time, and 4) the effect of physiological noise on functional networks can be reduced by applying a CompCor procedure to the BOLD time-series.
the effect of echo time on BOLD functional connectivity analysis is dependent on the type of post-processing applied.
the effect of echo time (TE), post-processing procedure and motion correction on the blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) signal functional connectivity analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of TE and post-processing on spontaneous BOLD fMR signal.
how echo time (TE), physiological noise correction and motion correction affect the detection of functional networks using BOLD fMRI data.
the effect of TE and post-processing on spontaneous BOLD fMR signal analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
R2*-derived data are less sensitive to physiological noise and motion, but TE and post-processing are important factors to consider when analyzing spontaneous BOLD data.

R2*-derived BOLD connectivity analysis is less affected by motion and confounding physiological noise and that the optimal TE for spontaneous BOLD f-MRI network detection depends on the post-processing procedure.
TE, post-processing and R2* are all important factors that must be considered in the interpretation of functional connectivity results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
R2* derived maps are less affected by motion and noise than BOLD data, while the intermediate TE (35ms) provides the best balance between signal to noise and sensitivity to physiological noise.

the R2*-based connectivity patterns are least affected by physiological noise confounds and motion, and thus may provide the best estimate of the true spontaneous BOLD functional connectivity patterns.
the BOLD data at 3T is not TE independent and that the BOLD signal is sensitive to motion and physiological noise, and that these effects can be reduced using appropriate post-processing.

the use of R2*-derived data is more robust to confounds and provides a better estimate of spontaneous BOLD connectivity.
the R2*-based connectivity analysis is less affected by physiological noise and motion, and provides a more reliable connectivity map than BOLD-based analysis.
